newsitem.title: USA: Wash. nuclear unit at full power, at least to Fri.
newsitem.headline: Wash. nuclear unit at full power, at least to Fri.

text.p: Washington Public Power Supply System's 1,158 megawatt (MW) nuclear unit near Richland, Wash., will run at full rates at least through Friday, a spokesman for the plant said Tuesday.
"Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) has requested that we stay at full power, without the load cycling that was implemented last week," spokesman Richard Romanelli said.

Monday through Friday of last week the unit ran at full power during 0700-2100 PST, but was brought down to 70 percent capacity through nighttime hours and the weekend due to an oversupply of lower-cost hydropower.
Operations at the nuclear unit were also curtailed for part of last week to correct a problem with a new adjustable speed drive system.
But recent cold weather led BPA, which markets the plant's electricity output, to request that WNP-2 remain at full power around the clock, Romanelli said.
The market situation will be reassessed after this weekend, he added.
